---
title: "Physical Activity & Depressive Symptoms"
subtitle: "A look at more than 5,000 U.S. adults in NHANES 2017–2018"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: article
---

## The question

How do recreational physical activity and depressive-symptom scores vary
together among adults? Each dot below represents one NHANES participant with
complete responses to the measures used here. The data are from a public
national health survey—not from college athletes—so this is a new topic, not a
claim about wrestlers or athletic performance.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(haven)

demo <- read_xpt("data/DEMO_J.XPT")
activity <- read_xpt("data/PAQ_J.XPT")
depression <- read_xpt("data/DPQ_J.XPT")

phq_items <- paste0("DPQ", sprintf("%03d", seq(10, 90, by = 10)))

minutes_per_week <- function(answer, days, minutes) {
  answer <- as.numeric(answer)
  days <- as.numeric(days)
  minutes <- as.numeric(minutes)

  answer[answer %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA_real_
  days[days %in% c(77, 99)] <- NA_real_
  minutes[minutes %in% c(7777, 9999)] <- NA_real_

  dplyr::case_when(
    answer == 2 ~ 0,
    answer == 1 & !is.na(days) & !is.na(minutes) & minutes <= 1440 ~ days * minutes,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )
}

plot_data <- demo |>
  inner_join(activity, by = "SEQN") |>
  inner_join(depression, by = "SEQN") |>
  filter(RIDAGEYR >= 18) |>
  mutate(
    across(all_of(phq_items), \(x) {
      x <- as.numeric(x)
      replace(x, x %in% c(7, 9), NA_real_)
    }),
    phq9 = rowSums(across(all_of(phq_items)), na.rm = FALSE),
    vigorous_minutes = minutes_per_week(PAQ650, PAQ655, PAD660),
    moderate_minutes = minutes_per_week(PAQ665, PAQ670, PAD675),
    recreational_mvpa = vigorous_minutes + moderate_minutes,
    sex = factor(RIAGENDR, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female"))
  ) |>
  filter(complete.cases(phq9, recreational_mvpa, sex))

stopifnot(nrow(plot_data) >= 2000)

activity_groups <- plot_data |>
  mutate(
    activity_group = case_when(
      recreational_mvpa == 0 ~ "0 minutes",
      recreational_mvpa < 150 ~ "1–149 minutes",
      recreational_mvpa < 300 ~ "150–299 minutes",
      TRUE ~ "300+ minutes"
    ),
    activity_group = factor(
      activity_group,
      levels = c("0 minutes", "1–149 minutes", "150–299 minutes", "300+ minutes")
    )
  )

group_counts <- activity_groups |>
  count(activity_group) |>
  mutate(activity_label = paste0(as.character(activity_group), "\n(n = ", n, ")"))

activity_groups <- activity_groups |>
  left_join(select(group_counts, activity_group, activity_label), by = "activity_group") |>
  mutate(activity_group = factor(activity_label, levels = group_counts$activity_label)) |>
  select(-activity_label)
```

The analysis includes **`r format(nrow(plot_data), big.mark = ",")` complete
adult responses**. Each point is one respondent; the curves summarize the
overall pattern within each sex category recorded in NHANES.

## Activity and symptom scores

The x-axis uses a square-root scale to make both zero and high activity values
visible. Vertical jitter separates overlapping scores; it does not change the
underlying scores. PHQ-9 scores range from 0 to 27, with higher scores
indicating more frequent depressive symptoms during the questionnaire's
reference period.

```{r}
#| label: fig-activity-symptoms
#| fig-cap: "Each point is a complete adult NHANES response. Smooth curves are descriptive; they do not establish cause and effect."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = recreational_mvpa, y = phq9, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.18,
    size = 0.9,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.12)
  ) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(sex), ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    trans = "sqrt",
    breaks = c(0, 30, 60, 150, 300, 600, 1200, 2400),
    labels = scales::label_number()
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 27, by = 3), limits = c(0, 27)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Male" = "#007C91", "Female" = "#B34E7A")) +
  labs(
    x = "Moderate + vigorous recreational activity (minutes per week)",
    y = "PHQ-9 depressive-symptom score",
    color = "NHANES sex category",
    caption = "Activity includes recreation only; work and transportation activity are not included."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

## Symptom-score distributions across activity groups

This second view compares the spread of scores across descriptive activity
groups. The violins show the distribution shape, boxplots show the median and
middle half, and faint points retain the individual observations. The
150-minute cutpoint is a plotting bin, not a claim that this leisure-only
measure is equivalent to a physical-activity guideline.

```{r}
#| label: fig-score-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Individual complete responses and score distributions by weekly recreational activity group."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5

ggplot(activity_groups, aes(x = activity_group, y = phq9, fill = activity_group)) +
  geom_violin(trim = TRUE, alpha = 0.65, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.16, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(
    color = "#243746",
    alpha = 0.12,
    size = 0.7,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0.12)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8CB4B8", "#5A9B9F", "#277B85", "#155B67")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 27, by = 3), limits = c(0, 27)) +
  labs(
    x = "Moderate + vigorous recreational activity per week",
    y = "PHQ-9 depressive-symptom score",
    title = "The score distributions overlap across activity groups",
    caption = "Group sample sizes appear below each label; all plotted points are individual respondents."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

These are exploratory, unweighted comparisons of survey responses. Activity
and mood may be related in complicated ways, and the plots cannot establish
that one causes the other. See [Data & methods](methods.qmd) for the source,
scoring choices, and limitations.
